comments.author: Aktillum
comments.content: Will your Quest creator ever feature support to create multiplayer text games? I'm highly addicted to multiplayer text games like Achaea. You'd probably call them MUDs but that's an archaic terminolgy as most text game developers could easily be considered MMORPGs nowadays. I hope you consider implementing multiplayer text game support.

comments.author: Alex Warren
comments.content:
It's a possibility for the future. I think the design of Quest is flexible enough that it could be adapted to multiplayer.

Back in the days of Quest 3 and 4, there was in fact a multiplayer version called QuestNet, but it never really attracted many users.

comments.author: julius
comments.content:
"There are more jobs than qualified developers out there"

-> could you please tell me where this huge number of hidden job opportunities for competent software developers are advertised? the main IT job sites seem to be looking only for people with large amounts of commercial experience doing exactly the same as the job in question. and it's not just the agencies being silly, it's clear employers give agencies a brief along the lines of "We want someone with x years experience with the following key words".

comments.author: Alex Warren
comments.content:
Job adverts often "inflate" the amount of experience required, because candidates often "inflate" the amount of experience they have, so it's a lose-lose situation really. It's not helped by HR-types meddling with the criteria and filtering CVs themselves, so you either have to play the game or hope that there's somebody technically competent at the other end reading your CV.

Then of course there's the fact that there are plenty of bogus listings out there - either recruiters simply looking to get as many CVs on their books as possible (possibly not such a bad thing if you're desparate for work, just be aware that recruiters will spam with you with anything that matches any words on your CV), or because a company has a vacancy it wants to fill with a particular individual but has to be seen to be advertising it externally for whatever reason.

Yes, IT recruitment completely sucks!

The other thing you can do is to give yourself some of that missing "essential" experience - there are plenty of open source projects you can actively contribute to (like Quest!), and for the employers you actually *want* to work for, that experience should count heavily in your favour. After all, most developers don't contribute to any open source projects at all, and when you do, you're giving potential employers a lot of information about how you work.
